mainEntity.name: Can functional medicine help anxiety and low mood?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We look at the physical drivers behind mood, the gut, blood sugar, thyroid, hormones, and nutrients, alongside your mental health care. Many people feel steadier as those root causes are addressed.

mainEntity.name: Do you replace my therapist or psychiatrist?

acceptedAnswer.text: We work alongside your mental health care. Our focus is the body side of mood, which is often overlooked.

mainEntity.name: What testing do you run for mood?

acceptedAnswer.text: We go beyond a basic panel, with thyroid, blood sugar, key nutrients, hormones, and inflammation markers, so the plan targets your specific root causes.

mainEntity.name: Can a physical problem really affect my mood?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Thyroid imbalance, blood sugar swings, nutrient gaps, and gut inflammation can all look and feel like anxiety or depression. We find and address them.

mainEntity.name: Will I have to stop my medication?

acceptedAnswer.text: Any changes to medication are made with your prescriber. We focus on the root-cause work that supports how you feel.

mainEntity.name: How soon might I notice a difference?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some people feel steadier within a few weeks as blood sugar and nutrients improve, while deeper change follows your body over time.

mainEntity.name: Do you offer virtual mood care or only in person in Atlanta?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both. See Dr. Nina Ross in person at our Atlanta clinic, or virtually anywhere in Georgia. Your $99 Symptom Consultation can be booked either way.

sections.label: Hero

headings.text: Root-cause anxiety and mood care in Atlanta that looks at the whole you.

paragraphs: If the anxiety, the low mood, the edginess and the sense that you are not quite yourself have crept in without a clear reason, you are not imagining it.

How you feel is real, and it deserves someone who will look at the whole story, body included. At Nina Ross Functional Medicine, we look at the root causes behind mood, here in Atlanta and virtually across Georgia. Dr. Nina Ross follows the whole picture, the gut, blood sugar, and hormones, to understand what is shaping how you feel, working alongside your mental health care, then builds the plan around your body and your life.

sections.label: Why conventional care misses it

headings.text: You were offered a prescription and the door.

eyebrowSpans: Why conventional care keeps missing it
paragraphs: A fifteen-minute visit rarely has room to ask what in the body might be shaping your mood. So how you feel gets met with a single prescription, and the physical drivers go unexamined.

boldPairs.title: What you’re usually told
boldPairs.body: “Let us try this medication and see how you feel in a few weeks.”

boldPairs.title: What’s actually happening
boldPairs.body: The gut, blood sugar, and hormones are influencing your brain in a loop. Steady the loop and mood often steadies with it.

sections.label: The functional medicine difference

headings.text: We will not treat your mind and ignore your body.

paragraphs: Here is where we part ways with conventional care. When mood suffers, the reflex answer is often a single prescription with little look at the body underneath. Medication helps many people, and it has its place. But the gut, blood sugar, thyroid, and nutrients all shape how you feel, and leaving them unexamined means a real driver can go unaddressed.
We would rather do the harder, more honest work. We look for what in your body is shaping how you feel and we address that, alongside your mental health care.
If medication and therapy have a place in your care, and for many people they do, that should be part of a full picture, with the body looked at too.

boldPairs.title: It treats the mind, not the whole you
boldPairs.body: Mood is shaped by the body too, so the gut, blood sugar, and hormones deserve a look.

boldPairs.title: A prescription can skip the cause
boldPairs.body: Medication can ease symptoms while a nutrient or thyroid driver goes unfound.

boldPairs.title: It works best alongside the body work
boldPairs.body: Addressing the physical drivers often makes everything else work better.

sections.label: The root-cause view

headings.text: Mood runs in a loop. We map the whole circle.

paragraphs: Each driver pushes the next. That is why treating one in isolation rarely holds, and why mapping the full cycle changes everything.
When we look at your mood, we read the whole picture rather than symptoms alone, and connect each driver back to what you’re feeling:

strongBullets.full: The gut-brain axis, where an inflamed gut quietly shapes anxiety and low mood.

strongBullets.label: Blood sugar swings
strongBullets.full: Blood sugar swings, behind the irritability, the shakiness, and the afternoon dip.

strongBullets.label: Thyroid function
strongBullets.full: Thyroid function, an imbalance that can look exactly like depression or anxiety.

strongBullets.label: Sex hormones
strongBullets.full: Sex hormones, the estrogen and progesterone shifts that move mood.

strongBullets.label: Nutrient gaps
strongBullets.full: Nutrient gaps, low B vitamins, vitamin D, omega-3s, and iron the brain needs.

strongBullets.label: Cortisol & stress
strongBullets.full: Cortisol & stress, a stress response stuck on that frays calm and sleep.

strongBullets.label: Chronic inflammation
strongBullets.full: Chronic inflammation, the quiet driver increasingly linked to mood.
